Download BDHS datasets with your DHS Program account (experimental)

Source: R/download.R
bdhs_download.Rd

Experimental. The DHS Program has no download API, so this function signs in to https://dhsprogram.com with your account and uses the website's download manager, as a browser would (the approach of the rdhs package). Website changes can break it at any time; the reliable route is to download the files yourself and run bdhs_import().

You can only download datasets that the DHS Program has approved for your project. Register at https://dhsprogram.com/data/new-user-registration.cfm and request access to the Bangladesh surveys first.

Usage

bdhs_download(
  survey,
  recode,
  format = "stata",
  email = Sys.getenv("DHS_EMAIL"),
  project = Sys.getenv("DHS_PROJECT"),
  import = TRUE,
  engine = c("bdhs", "rdhs")
)

Arguments

survey

Survey references (see bdhs_survey_id()).

recode

Recode codes (see bdhs_recodes()).

format

File format to download: "stata" (recommended), "spss" or "sas".

email

Email address of your DHS Program account.

project

Name of your approved DHS project.

import

If TRUE (default), import the downloaded files with bdhs_import(); bdhs's own downloader then deletes the downloaded zips. If FALSE, the zips are kept in a downloads folder of bdhs_data_dir() (you can import them later with bdhs_import()).

engine

"bdhs" (default) uses bdhs's own downloader (needs the httr2 package). "rdhs" delegates to rdhs::get_datasets(); configure rdhs first with rdhs::set_rdhs_config(). rdhs keeps the zips it downloads in its own cache folder (see rdhs::get_rdhs_config()), and bdhs leaves that cache alone, with import = TRUE as well: delete the cached copies yourself if you do not want two copies of the data.

Value

If import = TRUE, the registry rows of the imported datasets (see bdhs_import()); otherwise a tibble with the downloaded file_name and path. Invisibly.

Credentials

  • email and project default to the DHS_EMAIL and DHS_PROJECT environment variables (for example set in your .Renviron). project is the name of your approved DHS project (its first 30 characters are enough).

  • The password is taken from the system keyring when the keyring package is installed (service "bdhs-dhs", username = your email; store it once with keyring::key_set("bdhs-dhs", username = "you@example.org")), then from the DHS_PASSWORD environment variable, and is otherwise asked for at a hidden prompt in interactive sessions (this needs the askpass package; bdhs never asks for it with a prompt that shows what you type). bdhs never stores, prints or logs it, and does not keep it in options.

  • The password is only sent to https://dhsprogram.com: bdhs does not follow redirects of the sign-in form to other sites, and only follows download links that point to https://dhsprogram.com (or its subdomains).

In non-interactive sessions without credentials the function stops with instructions for downloading the files manually.

See also

Other data store: bdhs_data_dir(), bdhs_forget(), bdhs_identify_file(), bdhs_import(), bdhs_inventory(), bdhs_read(), bdhs_read_file(), bdhs_sitrep()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # interactive() && nzchar(Sys.getenv("DHS_EMAIL"))
bdhs_download(2022, c("IR", "KR"))
bdhs_read(2022, "KR", vars = "hw70")
}
